question: A nurse is teaching a client newly diagnosed with hypertension about lifestyle changes. Which statements by the client indicate correct understanding?

options.label: A
options.text: I will limit my sodium intake to less than 2,300 mg a day.

options.label: B
options.text: I should stop taking my blood pressure pill once it's normal.

options.label: C
options.text: I will try to get at least 150 minutes of exercise weekly.

options.label: D
options.text: I can keep smoking as long as I take my medication.

options.label: E
options.text: I will limit alcohol to no more than one drink a day.

options.label: F
options.text: Losing even a little weight can help lower my blood pressure.

explanation: Sodium restriction, regular aerobic exercise, moderate alcohol intake, and weight loss are all evidence-based lifestyle changes that lower blood pressure. Antihypertensive medication should never be stopped just because the pressure normalizes, and smoking must be addressed rather than excused by medication.
keyPoint: Lifestyle changes work together with medication; they don't replace it.
